title: Tumors may themselves emit bioelectric information detectable at a distance

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Tumors may themselves emit bioelectric information detectable at a distance

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors speculate that long-range bioelectric connections in tumorigenesis are bidirectional, so that in addition to remote tissue voltage influencing tumor growth, tumors may emit bioelectric information that could be detected at a distance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is tempting to speculate that the long-range connections are bi-directional: not only does remote electrical state of tissue matter for tumor growth, but perhaps tumors also emit bioelectrical information that could be detectable at a distance.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “DISCUSSION › Long-range control of tumorigenic process by Vmem”. Scope: Tumor–host bioelectric signaling, to be tested with molecular reagents in Xenopus and other models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-09: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is experimentally clear, but the existing experiments manipulate remote voltage and observe tumors rather than measuring signals emitted by tumors. New longitudinal bioelectric data are required.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map Vmem at defined distances and times before and after inducing tumors, then remove or inhibit tumors and test whether remote electrical signatures disappear. A reproducible tumor-specific remote signal would support bidirectionality.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public spatial Vmem time series paired with tumor induction is identified.

The source presents this as future work.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.75
data existence: 0.1
operationalizability: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Outward bioelectric emission is testable once a remote signal and a disconnection control are defined, which the speculation leaves open. No deposited recording set contains that pair for the Xenopus structures or a mammalian counterpart. The detection claim therefore waits on new measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Record bioelectric signals at a distance from induced tumors, with connectivity intact and interrupted, and test whether a remote signature predicts tumor state and disappears when the path is cut. A connectivity-dependent remote signature would support outward emission; no remote signal above controls would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public dataset pairs remote non-neural voltage with these induced structures.

The emitted signal and the distance at which it should be detectable are unspecified.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.12
